question.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & -6 \\ 4 & 5 & -12 \\ 3 & 3 & -7\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,C-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
C-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 3 & -6 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda  & -12 \\ 3 & 3 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(C-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 3 & -6 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda  & -12 \\ 3 & 3 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -12 \\ 3 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}|-3|\begin{aligned}4 & -12 \\ 3 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}|+(-6)|\begin{aligned}4 & 5-\lambda  \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +1)-3(-4\lambda +8)-6(-3+3\lambda ) & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}+7\lambda +4)-(-12\lambda +24)-(-18+18\lambda ) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda +2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
